queue.title: NEM Test report delivery: brand the covering email and the PDF report
queue.description: In the /verify n8n workflow (nem-verify.workflow.json), style the two visual surfaces of report delivery. (1) Send Report node (MailerSend): the covering email is currently plain text only — add a branded html body using table-based layout and inline styles so it renders across email clients including Outlook, keeping the existing text as the plain-text fallback. (2) Build HTML node: upgrade the report HTML that PDFShift renders into the attached PDF — add NEM logo header, brand colours, and layout for the mechanism scores, using modern CSS (Chromium engine allows flexbox, web fonts, @page margins). Support NL and EN locales for both surfaces. Re-import the workflow into n8n after editing (or apply live via the n8n MCP if deployed).
queue.note: Spec written 2026-08-11: projects/nem-life/.claude/specs/nem-verify-report-email-and-pdf-branding.md. The report chain works but looks like a debug fixture - the covering email is one line of plain text with no HTML part at all, and the PDF is an unbranded serif document with no logo, colour or footer. Brand both to NEM Life (calm, warm-neutral, muted olive/gold accent). Touches Build HTML and Send Report only. Three defects found while specifying: (1) Build HTML does paragraph splitting and no markdown handling, so any ## heading, **bold** or - list in Alex's real prompt output will print as literal characters - latent today only because the stub returns flat prose; (2) the PDF filename is hardcoded NEM-rapport.pdf even for EN users; (3) email analytics read 0.00% opened because there is no HTML part for a tracking pixel to live in - adding one is a precondition for any delivery reporting. SEQUENCING: land nem-report-prompt-escaping-and-token-limit (P0) first, then RE-PULL LIVE before editing - both tasks edit the same workflow and n8n has no version history, so editing from a stale copy silently destroys the other's work. Colour tokens are NOT in the repo (global.css yields only a stray #4d65ff); pull them from the Webflow site variables or Figma 8jRJkSvjuMQzYkA1gXc646 before writing CSS. Open question for Alex: should the email carry a link back to the site? Clicks are the trustworthy half of the analytics and there is nothing to click while the report is a bare attachment.

queue.title: NEM Test report prompt: make the prompt safe to edit and lift the token limit
queue.description: In the live /verify workflow the Anthropic system prompt is a single-quoted JavaScript string literal inside the Generate Report node's jsonBody expression, so the first apostrophe or newline in Alex's real prompt breaks the node silently (the browser already got its 302). Move the prompt into a Report Prompt Set node as a plain fixed-value string so JSON.stringify handles all escaping. Also lift max_tokens from the live value of 1024 to the intended 8000, switch $json references to explicit $('Validate Token') references, and re-sync the repo workflow JSON to live. Prerequisite for any mechanism that lets the client edit the prompt himself.
queue.note: APPLIED TO LIVE 2026-08-13, CONFIRMED 2026-08-18. The 2026-08-11 note below was wrong by the time anyone read it: the fix was applied by hand in the n8n UI on 13 Aug (workflow updatedAt 15:03:50Z; execution 45 at 15:02 already shows Report Prompt in its path), so no commit in this repo recorded it and every doc still said PREPARED, NOT APPLIED. Found by taking the pre-apply snapshot: the live pull came back with a node the repo copy did not have. DO NOT re-send partial-update.operations.json - it would add a second Report Prompt node or fail. Verified live: Report Prompt is a Set node typeVersion 3.5 with no legacy parameters.fields, holding systemPrompt as a fixed value that does not start with '='; Valid? true branch fans out to Respond Confirmed, Mark Consumed and Report Prompt so the 302 does not wait on the report chain; Generate Report reads the Set node, uses $('Validate Token') references and max_tokens 8000. The repo workflow JSON has been re-synced from the API. The old n8n API key blocker is also gone - the key works. STILL OUTSTANDING and tracked elsewhere: systemPrompt holds a clearly-labelled TEST MODE stub, so live reports read 'TESTRAPPORT / TEST REPORT'; installing Alex's real prompt is blocked on Notion access.

queue.title: Report delivery is failing in production: MailerSend is on a trial account
queue.description: Executions 30 and 35 on 2026-07-09 both failed at Send Report with 422 'You have reached trial account unique recipients limit. #MS42225'. Report generation, PDF render and encode all succeed; only delivery fails. Because Mark Consumed sits on the fast path, the token is consumed anyway, so the user sees the confirmed page, never receives a report, and cannot retry. Add To Newsletter also never runs, so consenting users are not subscribed. Blocked on Alex upgrading the MailerSend account off trial. Once unblocked, consider whether Mark Consumed should move back behind successful delivery, and add failure alerting to the report branch so silent failures surface. Corrects the backend README, which currently states MailerSend is production and that no credential work blocks go-live.
queue.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-18. Alex upgraded the MailerSend account to a paid 'Hobby' plan and offered to go higher if volume needs it. Verified end-to-end rather than taken on trust: inserted one nem_test_profiles row with a fresh token and a never-before-used recipient, fired GET /verify?token=..., and execution 48 ran all 14 nodes green including Send Report, with the report email arriving at 10:14:42Z. Probe row deleted afterwards. Testing with an already-seen address would have passed regardless, since the cap was on unique recipients - always probe with a new address. Two follow-ups this ticket raised are NOT done and are tracked elsewhere: (1) whether Mark Consumed should move back behind successful delivery, so a delivery failure leaves the token replayable instead of stranding the user - still on the fast path, still worth a decision; (2) failure alerting on the report branch, now specced in projects/nem-life/.claude/specs/nem-report-json-and-error-visibility.md. New thing to watch: the Hobby plan caps monthly volume rather than recipients, and reports plus failure alerts share the account, so hitting the quota silences both at once.

queue.title: Stop the NEM docs going stale about live n8n
queue.description: Docs asserted live n8n state with no way to tell when anyone last checked, and three stale-claim failures landed in one week: the prompt-escaping changeset was applied by hand on 13 Aug while every doc still said PREPARED NOT APPLIED and the committed workflow JSON was missing a node; the MailerSend trial cap was recorded as a live blocker across seven files after it had been lifted; and the n8n API key blocker was stale too. Built tools/nem/check-workflow-drift.js (npm run check:nem-drift) which pulls both live workflows, diffs them against the committed snapshots, names the field that moved, checks a set of invariants, and exits non-zero. Never auto-syncs: drift ran in both directions, so an auto-fix would have destroyed real work. Generates backend/LIVE-STATE.md as the one place allowed to assert live state. Established a doc convention at the top of backend/README.md: dated Verified stamps, link to LIVE-STATE rather than restating node params, and strike through cleared blockers instead of deleting them.
queue.note: Done 2026-08-18. 33 new tests, suite now 160 passing. Audit found /submit drifting in three nodes in BOTH directions: Store Profile was a stale pre-deployment template (insert + REPLACE_DATA_TABLE_ID vs live upsert on the real table), while the repo was AHEAD of live on MailerLite status:'active' and on a corrected $env comment in Normalize. Snapshots re-baselined from live per Will's decision; the two repo-ahead items raised as nem-mailerlite-subscriber-status-active and nem-submit-normalize-comment-drift, both P3. The check needs N8N_API_KEY so it cannot run in plain CI - it is a before-you-work command. If it starts getting skipped, a pre-work hook is the next step, not CI.

queue.title: JSON report contract and Parse Report validation branch
queue.description: Slice 1 of nem-report-json-and-error-visibility (spec sections 1-3), planned 2026-08-18. Claude returns report content as strict JSON with five keys (opening, reaction, origin, cost, closing); a Parse Report Code node becomes the only place that output is trusted or rejected, failing on not-json, missing-key, empty-value and truncated. Failures write a row to a new nem_report_failures Data Table and email Alex; Send Report must not fire, so nobody receives a half-built PDF. CRITICAL COUPLING: the live Report Prompt currently holds a TEST MODE stub that returns PROSE, so shipping Parse Report on its own would route every real user to the failure branch. The stub must be rewritten to emit the JSON contract in the SAME apply. Will's call 2026-08-18: rewrite the stub, so the chain is exercisable now and Alex's real prompt later drops in like-for-like. Alert rides the same MailerSend account as the reports - accepted as a known single point of failure rather than over-built for an unmeasured failure rate.
queue.note: BUILT AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-18. Exec 49 (happy path): Parse Report valid, five sections through Build HTML, Send Report succeeded. Exec 50 (failure path, stub temporarily pointed at prose): reason not-json, row written to nem_report_failures, Alert Alex fired, and Send Report DID NOT RUN - the assertion that matters, since a half-built PDF is worse than none. Stub restored immediately afterwards and both probe rows deleted. 44 unit tests; suite now 199. The validator necessarily exists twice (module + pasted Code node, since n8n cannot import), so the tests extract the node's real source from the committed snapshot and run it against the same fixtures - edit the module, re-paste, re-baseline, never only the node. Three new drift invariants guard the gate: the prompt still demands JSON, Generate Report goes through Parse Report, and the failure branch cannot reach Build HTML or Send Report. NOTE: testing the failure path sent a real alert email to alex@nemlife.com at 13:23 - point Alert Alex at your own address next time.

queue.title: /submit silently drops the v2 outcome, conclusionKey and conclusionId
queue.description: The conclusion engine v2 component sends outcome, conclusionKey and conclusionId in the submit payload, but /submit's Normalize node does not map any of them and nem_test_profiles has no columns for them, so all three are discarded.
